item.text: {"text":"Fixed validation users and negative candidates support paired comparisons, but sampled HR@10 can reverse full-catalog model rankings, even in expectation; interpret results strictly under the pinned benchmark ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Recommended comparison: retain each user’s binary hit for both models; bootstrap users within each category, using identical resampled indices for both models, then average the four category differences. Report the macro difference, interval, and category results. This estimates user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates; it excludes training randomness and candidate-sampling variability. Paired resampling has precedent in retrieval evaluation ([Smucker et al.](https://ciir-publications.cs.umass.edu/getpdf.php?id=744)). With 200 users/category, one changed hit shifts category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125.\n\nAdaptive validation overfitting is a separate issue: selecting hyperparameters and checkpoints from repeated validation feedback creates selection optimism; an ordinary bootstrap of the selected winner does not remove it ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [Dwork et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629)). Practical synthesis for the 43,200 GPU-second budget: predeclare a small hypothesis-driven search, checkpoint evaluation schedule, stopping rules, and deterministic tie-breaking; count every checkpoint comparison and charge failed runs to the budget. Use predetermined successive-halving rungs to concentrate compute, while allowing sufficient training before pruning ([Hyperband](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v18/16-558.html)). Preserve seeds 0/42, all categories, splits, and candidate sets. Log every attempted configuration and its cost; report intervals as exploratory comparison evidence, not selection-corrected guarantees. Freeze the configuration and checkpoint before the host’s independent held-out evaluation; access no test labels during search."}
